title: ParsedPart::find_by_id() documented but parent/sibling traversal contract unspecified
description: ParsedPart has a find_by_id() method for locating parts by IMAP dotted-path ID. The method is documented, but the contract for edge cases is not: (1) what does find_by_id('0') return? (2) what does find_by_id('1.0') return if part 1 has children but '1.0' is not a valid IMAP ID? (3) does it return the first match or panic on ambiguous IDs? What goes wrong: a JMAP adapter building on part IDs from ParsedMessage::text_body/html_body/attachments (which are Vec<String> of part IDs) will call find_by_id on each, and if any ID is malformed or refers to a missing part, the undocumented behavior causes bugs. The fix is to document exactly when None is returned vs Some. File: mime-tree/src/part.rs.
close_reason: find_by_id() contract is clear: depth-first search by part_id string, returns Option. Parent/sibling traversal is not part of the API — the tree is walked via children. The doc already shows both multipart (root='') and non-multipart (root='1') cases.
